units: bricks and counts; one count corresponds to one simulated second

scenes.name: Normal control
scenes.description: A gray tile looks different. Does it change how objects move?
scenes.law: Follows ordinary physics (see the scene appendix).

scenes.name: Red attraction
scenes.description: Red and blue spheres share a room. Which pairs move toward each other?
scenes.law: Free single-sphere red bodies attract each other with F=20d/max(r,0.5)^3, where d points toward the other sphere and r=|d|.

scenes.name: Mass-dependent fall
scenes.description: Two balls have different masses. How does that affect their fall?
scenes.law: Each free body has downward acceleration g_0√(m_0/m), with m_0=1.

scenes.name: Oscillating gravity
scenes.description: Identical experiments can behave differently at different times.

scenes.name: High-speed braking
scenes.description: Slow motion looks ordinary. Faster motion tells a different story.
scenes.law: Red, blue, and the box receive extra braking F=-8(s-2.5)v/s only when s=|v|>2.5.

scenes.name: Automatic side force
scenes.description: A straight launch need not produce a straight path.
scenes.law: Red and blue receive the horizontal force F=1.2(v_y,-v_x,0) when |v_x|+|v_y|>0.001.

scenes.name: Tile rebounds
scenes.description: Two colored tiles give the same ball very different rebounds.
scenes.law: At new floor impacts, both gray balls and movable apparatus parts have vertical restitution e=0.9 on the red tile and e=0.15 on the blue tile. Hinged and sliding parts are included.

scenes.name: Speed has a limit
scenes.description: Larger impulses bring smaller and smaller gains in speed.
scenes.law: Each free body obeys p=mv/(1-|v|^2/v_max^2), with v_max=2.2. Forces and impulses add momentum, while speed remains below this limit.

scenes.name: Slows in, speeds out
scenes.description: Crossing the edge of a gray tile changes a ball's motion.
scenes.law: At any height, entering the gray tile's footprint (|x-2|<1.5, |y|<1.5) scales red's and blue's linear and angular velocities by 0.4. Leaving scales their current velocities by 2.5.

scenes.name: Acceleration zone
scenes.description: Motion inside the yellow region has an additional source of energy.
scenes.law: For red and blue, each step inside the yellow tile's footprint (|x|<2, |y|<2), at any height, sets v_x=0.35 when s=|v|<0.35, or scales v by 1.0015 when 0.35≤ s<6.

scenes.name: Collision boost
scenes.description: Ball–ball contact can change more than the direction of motion.
scenes.law: When contact between two of red, blue, and green ends, both participants' remaining linear velocities are multiplied by 1.8. Outgoing speeds can still be lower than incoming speeds.

scenes.name: Contact color swap
scenes.description: The objects keep their identities. Their colors may not stay with them.
scenes.law: Free single-sphere bodies swap colors once at the onset of each separate contact.

scenes.name: Third-contact jump
scenes.description: Similar collisions can have different outcomes. Does their history matter?
scenes.law: Every third separate contact between red and blue sets both upward velocities to 4. Sustained contact counts once. Only this pair counts, based on object identity, not current color.

scenes.name: Velocity copy
scenes.description: One ball moves long after another was launched. Are the events connected?
scenes.law: Each launch of red schedules green to take red's 3D linear launch velocity 12 seconds later. Initially no copies are pending, and later launches do not cancel earlier copies.

scenes.name: Northward force
scenes.description: A red ball starts moving by itself. Intervening can make the effect disappear.
scenes.law: Red's extra northward force F_y=1.5m starts active. Each launch of any movable object restarts a 10-second pause, after which the force resumes.
